paper_id: Yang and Liu - 2008 - Quality of Trilateration Confidence Based Iterative Localization
title: Quality of Trilateration: Confidence based Iterative Localization
motivation: Trilateration suffers poor accuracy due to noisy ranging, dynamic environments, and wireless fluctuations, making it hard to employ in practical applications.
problem_framing: Noisy distance measurement degrades trilateration in four aspects: uncertainty, non-consistency, ambiguity (flip), and error propagation.
key_insight: Different geometric forms of trilaterations provide different localization accuracy; QoT quantifies this relationship.
method_signature: QoT defines trilateration quality as probability mass within a disk around the estimated position, integrating geometric relationship and ranging noise.
evaluation_criteria: Localization accuracy and error propagation speed; validated via prototype experiments and large-scale simulations (600 nodes).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Location refinement may degrade 20% of nodes, but deterioration is small compared to improvement.
evidence_for_taste: reduces the likelihood of using low confidence references
fail to determine which combination of references provides accurate localization
thinking_moves: 把几何不确定性重新 frame 成可量化的概率质量问题
将confidence从二元判断扩展为连续值传播机制
用optimal substructure证明将问题转化为bellman-ford最短路问题
先通过prototype验证QoT有效性，再做大规模仿真验证scalability
